filter_params: key='.A.' (REF_AREA wildcard; FREQ=A; NOC wildcard — single-dimension dataset, no SEX/AGE breakdown). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . FREQ.
transform: none — value is already % of GDP
notes: Labour income share as % of GDP — ILO modelled estimates (SDG 10.4.1 primary input). Dataflow confirmed on DBnomics (271 series, 271 countries, annual, 2004–2020+). Identical to existing IL-02 spec in the fetcher: dataflow=SDG_1041_NOC_RT covers the same concept via the SDG-labelled dataflow; LAP_2GDP_NOC_RT is the direct ILO dataset code. RECOMMENDATION: prefer SDG_1041_NOC_RT (already confirmed live in IL-02) — use LAP_2GDP_NOC_RT as fallback if SDG_1041_NOC_RT is absent.

filter_params: key='.A.SEX_T' (REF_AREA wildcard; SOURCE wildcard; SEX=SEX_T total; FREQ=A). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . SEX . FREQ.
transform: none — value is rate (%); aggregate multiple source vintages by taking max-coverage (latest) observation per country-year
notes: Informal employment rate by sex, total (%). Dataflow confirmed on DBnomics: 688 series, 140 reference areas, 2004–2022. Country-specific labour force surveys as source (SOURCE dimension varies per country). Pull SEX_T for the total rate. Note this is a survey-based indicator (not modelled), so country coverage is uneven — expect gaps for low-income countries. Existing fetcher uses SDG_0831_SEX_ECO_RT (SDG 8.3.1 proxy for informality via sector); EMP_NIFL_SEX_RT is the direct informal-employment-rate dataset without the sector breakdown, making it the cleaner single series per country.

filter_params: key='.A.AGE_5YRBANDS_Y15-19+AGE_5YRBANDS_Y20-24.SEX_T' OR '.A.AGE_5YRBANDS_TOTAL.SEX_T'. DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . AGE . SEX . FREQ. Preferred slice: AGE_5YRBANDS_TOTAL (all youth 15–24 aggregate) + SEX_T. If AGE_5YRBANDS_TOTAL unavailable, sum Y15-19 and Y20-24 bands weighted by population (requires external denominator) — simpler to use total-age slice directly.
transform: none — value is rate (%). If only band-level data present, take average of Y15-19 and Y20-24 as approximation.
notes: Share of youth not in employment, education or training (NEET rate), by sex and age, %. Survey-based (LFS and household surveys). Confirmed on DBnomics: 1,952 series, 144 countries, annual. SDG 8.6.1 custodian indicator. IMPORTANT: this is a DISTINCT dataset from the existing IL-11 which uses EES_TNEE_SEX_AGE_RT (ILO modelled estimates). EIP_NEET_SEX_AGE_RT is survey-based (patchier coverage, more recent years) while EES_TNEE provides broader country coverage via modelling. For QGI ML use EES_TNEE_SEX_AGE_RT (IL-11) as primary; EIP_NEET_SEX_AGE_RT adds observed survey data where available. Age band codes confirmed: AGE_5YRBANDS_Y15-19, AGE_5YRBANDS_Y20-24, AGE_5YRBANDS_TOTAL.

filter_params: key='.A.SOC_AGGREGATE_ATLEAST1.SEX_T' (REF_AREA wildcard; SOURCE wildcard; SOC=SOC_AGGREGATE_ATLEAST1 = covered by at least one benefit; SEX=SEX_T total; FREQ=A). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . SOC . SEX . FREQ. Confirmed SOC code from existing IL-08 spec in fetcher.
transform: none — value is % of population covered
notes: Proportion of population covered by social protection floors/systems (%) — SDG 1.3.1. Dataflow confirmed on DBnomics: 2,769 series, 249 countries, annual. SOC dimension distinguishes contingency types (pension, maternity, disability, work-injury, poverty) plus the aggregate SOC_AGGREGATE_ATLEAST1. This dataset is IDENTICAL to existing IL-08 in the fetcher — same dataflow, same key. The panel code SDG_0131_SEX_SOC_RT is the raw dataflow ID (not a synthetic name). Treat as IL-08 alias; no new fetch logic needed.

filter_params: key='.A.ECO_AGGREGATE_TOTAL' (REF_AREA wildcard; SOURCE wildcard; ECO=ECO_AGGREGATE_TOTAL = all industries; FREQ=A). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . ECO . FREQ. NOTE: the panel uses synthetic code STR_NWRK_NOC_NB but the real ILOSTAT dataflow ID is STR_WORK_ECO_NB (confirmed on DBnomics; STR_NWRK_NOC_NB returns 404).
transform: none — value is thousands of workers
notes: Workers involved in strikes and lockouts by economic activity (thousands). Real dataflow: STR_WORK_ECO_NB (not STR_NWRK_NOC_NB — panel code is synthetic). Confirmed on DBnomics: 3,506 series, 124 reference areas, annual data. ECO_AGGREGATE_TOTAL sums across all industries. Sparse coverage — industrial relations data is voluntarily reported; many countries missing. Value in thousands. For a rate per 1,000 employees, divide by total employment (EMP_TEMP_SEX_ECO_NB total) — not done here.

filter_params: key='.A.ECO_AGGREGATE_TOTAL' (REF_AREA wildcard; SOURCE wildcard; ECO=ECO_AGGREGATE_TOTAL; FREQ=A). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . ECO . FREQ. NOTE: panel code STR_DAYS_NOC_NB is synthetic; real ILOSTAT dataflow is STR_DAYS_ECO_NB (confirmed on DBnomics).
transform: none — value is total working days lost (absolute count)
notes: Days not worked due to strikes and lockouts by economic activity (total days). Real dataflow: STR_DAYS_ECO_NB (not STR_DAYS_NOC_NB — panel code is synthetic). Confirmed on DBnomics: 3,586 series, 118 reference areas, annual. Absolute working-day count. Very sparse outside Europe/Americas. Compare to ILR_STR_NOC_RT (IL-13 in existing fetcher) which gives the rate per 1,000 employees — this dataset gives the raw total. Both are useful; this one is the headline total.

filter_params: key='.A.' (REF_AREA wildcard; SOURCE wildcard; FREQ=A; NOC — no classification dimension). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . FREQ.
notes: Trade union density rate (%) — share of employees who are trade union members. Dataflow confirmed on DBnomics: 139 reference areas, annual, sources include LFS, administrative records, and union membership registers. NOC = no classification breakdown (single rate per country-year). Sparse for sub-Saharan Africa and parts of Asia. This is the industrial relations union density indicator; pairs with ILR_CBCT_NOC_RT (collective bargaining coverage) if needed.

filter_params: key='.A.SEX_T' (REF_AREA wildcard; SOURCE wildcard; SEX=SEX_T total; FREQ=A). DSD: REF_AREA . SOURCE . SEX . FREQ.
notes: Low pay rate by sex (%) — share of employees earning below 2/3 of median hourly earnings. Dataflow confirmed on DBnomics: 70 reference areas, 89 source series, annual, 1996–2022. This is an earnings distribution indicator, not a poverty rate. Very limited coverage: primarily OECD/Europe economies where earnings microdata surveys exist. Expect <50 country-year observations for non-OECD. Value is the total-sex low pay rate; male and female breakdowns available via SEX_M / SEX_F if needed.
